title: Daily Market Digest: July 24, 2026
subtitle: Markets closed mixed on Friday amid tech weakness and geopolitical concerns.

items.headline: Wall Street Ends Week Mixed, Tech Under Pressure
items.summary: U.S. equities saw a mixed close on Friday, July 24, 2026, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average posting gains while the Nasdaq Composite continued its decline, primarily driven by concerns over substantial AI spending and ongoing geopolitical tensions. Oil prices retreated for the first time in a week, offering some relief to inflation fears, yet overall market sentiment remained cautious.

items.headline: Tenet Healthcare Soars on Strong Earnings
items.summary: Tenet Healthcare Corporation surged by 17.08% after reporting a strong second-quarter earnings beat, raising its full-year profit outlook, and showcasing robust performance in its ambulatory surgery network.

items.headline: SLB Jumps on Q2 Profit Beat
items.summary: Oilfield services firm SLB climbed 11% after exceeding expectations for its second-quarter profit, benefiting from higher energy prices.

items.headline: Salesforce Shows Strength Amid Tech Sell-off
items.summary: Salesforce saw a notable increase of 4.34% on Friday, standing out amidst broader tech sector weakness.

items.headline: SanDisk Corporation Plunges with Memory Stocks
items.summary: SanDisk Corporation dropped nearly 11% as memory stocks faced significant selling pressure, contributing to the broader tech sector's decline.

items.headline: Intel Shares Decline Despite Earnings Beat
items.summary: Intel shares declined 6.5% as investors focused on the company's plans for increased capital expenditures over the next two years, despite reporting a beat on adjusted Q2 earnings and strong revenue growth.

items.headline: American Express Disappoints with Q2 Revenue
items.summary: American Express fell 4.87% after reporting weaker-than-expected second-quarter revenue, adding to investor caution.

items.headline: Key Economic Data Released
items.summary: Friday's economic calendar included the release of July's Flash PMI data for both manufacturing and services, offering early insights into business activity for Q3. Additionally, new home sales figures and the Kansas City Fed Services Survey provided further updates on housing demand and regional service sector performance. Initial jobless claims decreased by 2,000 to 207,000 for the week ending July 18, while continuing claims also fell.

items.headline: AI Spending Raises Investor Concerns in Tech Sector
items.summary: Investor sentiment in the technology sector continues to be weighed down by concerns over mounting capital expenditures related to artificial intelligence. This comes after Alphabet Inc. ($GOOGL) reported strong Q2 earnings but raised its 2026 capex forecast, and Tesla ($TSLA) cited a 'massive capex year' ahead, leading to a significant weekly decline for the EV maker.

items.headline: Oil Prices Retreat Amid Middle East Tensions and New Tariffs
items.summary: Brent crude prices fell almost 4% on Friday, settling at $96.78 a barrel, after a week that saw prices climb above $100. This slight ease in crude prices provided some relief to inflation concerns, though continued geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and new tariffs imposed by President Trump on 60 global economies kept investors cautious.

items.headline: ECB Signals Potential September Rate Hike
items.summary: ECB President Christine Lagarde laid the groundwork for a potential interest rate hike in September, citing upside risks to inflation. This comes as markets continue to assess the impact of rising energy costs and global economic conditions on central bank policy.
